title: Sold by date
prompt: Show each order_date, the number of different products sold as products, and their names in alphabetical order with no repeats as names, sorted by date.
hints: Join, then use DISTINCT in both.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (14, 8, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (14, 8, 1, NULL), (14, 7, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT o.order_date, COUNT(DISTINCT p.name) AS products, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT p.name ORDER BY p.name) AS names FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY o.order_date ORDER BY o.order_date;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT o.order_date, COUNT(p.name) AS products, GROUP_CONCAT(p.name ORDER BY p.name) AS names FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY o.order_date ORDER BY o.order_date;

SELECT o.order_date, COUNT(DISTINCT p.name) AS products, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT p.name) AS names FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY o.order_date ORDER BY o.order_date;

title: Valid work emails
prompt: A valid email starts with a letter, then has only letters, digits, underscores, dots, or dashes, then ends with exactly @acme.test in lowercase. Show the id, name, and email of employees with one.
hints: Anchor both ends, and escape the dot.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET email = '9kim@acme.test' WHERE id = 13; UPDATE employees SET email = 'mia@ACME.test' WHERE id = 15; UPDATE employees SET email = 'leo@acmeXtest' WHERE id = 14;

solutions: SELECT id, name, email FROM employees WHERE email REGEXP '^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*@acme\.test$';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, name, email FROM employees WHERE email REGEXP '@acme\.test$';
SELECT id, name, email FROM employees WHERE email LIKE '%@acme.test';
wrongSolutions.why: LIKE ignores capitals and allows any start
